case: 100 purchased, 80 assigned, 40 active-30-day CRM seats; potential replacement has lower price but unknown migration costs. Separate licensing/adoption, do not count assigned as active, defer net-savings claim and separate locked renewal opportunity.
required_methods: Build an as-of spend inventory with contracts, category by actual job, annual/period costs, purchased seats, assigned seats and active-30-day seats. Without actual usage, do not claim idle-seat savings; retain seasonal/episodic use context.

Distinguish over-licensing from adoption failure. Compare utilization using appropriate cadence and owner-approved assumptions; upstream buffers and category percentages are scenarios, not company policy.

Compare overlapping tools by required capability, criticality, actual users and availability. Broad category labels do not prove substitutability. Select the proposed survivor using migration, displacement, disruption and exit cost as well as price; missing cost evidence limits savings claims.

Derive contractual notice deadlines, renewal windows, true-down rights and locked commitments. Separate gross opportunity, realizable this cycle and locked/future savings; rank time-sensitive opportunities before their leverage expires.

Produce an evidence-backed shortlist with sensitivity, execution owner, dependencies and approval requests. Right-size before considering term-extension discounts; do not cancel, change seats, serve notice or commit purchases without the actual approved action.
